articles.title: Skyrocketing fuel costs drive sharp decline in Nepali air travel
articles.summary:
Costly jet fuel in Nepal has forced domestic carriers to hike airfares by up to 40 percent, causing passenger numbers to plunge.

Escalating geopolitical tensions—driven by joint US and Israeli military operations in Iran—have sent global aviation fuel prices skyrocketing.

According to data compiled by domestic airlines and Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal (CAAN), the number of domestic passengers plunged by over 540,000 in the fiscal year 2025-26, which ended on July 16, mainly due to fuel price hike.

The data shows that total internal passenger traffic dropped 12 percent compared to the fiscal year 2024-25. Numbers fell from 4,557,634 passengers in the 2024-25 fiscal year to 4,016,880 in 2025-26—a net loss of 540,754 travellers.

The slump was particularly severe during the final five months of the fiscal year, from February to July. Monthly figures show passenger volume shrank by 10 percent in the Nepali month of Falgun (mid-February to mid-March), 17 percent in mid-March to mid-April, 33 percent in mid-April to mid-May, 34 percent in mid-May to mid-June, and 29 percent in mid-June to mid-July.

“The direct shock of the international energy crisis hit our domestic sector squarely during this period,” said Yubaraj Bista, chief business officer at Yeti Airlines. “While flight numbers in the first six months remained steady, the sudden spike in fuel costs made air travel unaffordable for ordinary citizens and domestic tourists.”

The downturn hit all major domestic carriers, including Buddha Air, Yeti Airlines, and Shree Airlines. Buddha Air experienced the largest numerical loss, dropping 394,000 passengers—a 14 percent decline that accounted for nearly 73 percent of the industry’s total drop.

Despite the contraction, Buddha Air maintained its market lead with a 58.3 percent share. Yeti Airlines lost 93,048 passengers (a 9 percent decline), holding a 22.5 percent market share, while Shree Airlines proved relatively resilient with a modest 6 percent drop.

Industry leaders warn that the financial strain threatens carrier solvency. Pratap Jung Pandey, president of the Airlines Operators Association of Nepal (AOAN) and operator of Kailash Helicopter, described the situation as critical.

“This is the second major crisis facing Nepali aviation since the Covid-19 pandemic,” said Pandey. “Balance sheets across several airlines have turned negative, and many operators are finding it difficult simply to survive.”

According to Pandey, operational costs have escalated further due to currency depreciation. “Fuel prices remain high and volatile,” he said. “Crucially, fees paid by airlines to CAAN are denominated in US dollars, as are spare parts, yet our income is entirely in Nepali rupees.”

The helicopter sector has felt a similar pinch, with flight hours down 20 to 30 percent across Nepal’s 11 helicopter operators.

The passenger decline spanned nearly every major airport in Nepal. Simara experienced the steepest drop at 24 percent, followed by Bhairahawa at 22 percent. Traffic at Pokhara shrank by 11 percent, while Nepalgunj fell by 16 percent. Dhangadhi dropped 13 percent, Surkhet 15 percent, and Rajbiraj 10 percent. Biratnagar and Bhadrapur each saw 7 percent decreases, while Janakpur recorded a 6 percent decline.

Nepal’s domestic aviation market relies on roughly 4 to 4.5 million passengers annually. Around 300,000 are foreign tourists, 300,000 Indian visitors, and 100,000 employees of Nepal government and non-governmental organisations. The remaining 3.9 million journeys are made by ordinary Nepalis travelling once or twice a year for family visits, medical treatment, or social obligations.

“When airfares rose, these occasional domestic travellers simply chose not to fly,” Bista explained. “Additionally, following recent political changes, daily market tracking shows a noticeable reduction in political leaders and cadres travelling to and from Kathmandu.”

Domestic airlines in Nepal faced compounding challenges over the past year, including rising insurance premiums and stringent regulatory safety audits. The added burden of fuel price volatility has further squeezed operational margins across the board.

In response to the crisis, airline representatives recently met with CAAN Director General Mukesh Dangol to seek government intervention. The AOAN representatives pointed out that while CAAN and the International Civil Aviation Organisation closely monitor technical safety, no state mechanism addresses the financial viability of domestic airlines, leaving operators exposed during external economic shocks.

articles.title: Chinese envoy voices concerns over upcoming Tibetan studies seminar in Kathmandu
articles.summary:
Chinese Ambassador to Nepal Zhang Maoming has expressed concerns over the upcoming 17th Seminar of the International Association for Tibetan Studies to be organised from August 23-29 in Kathmandu.

Ambassador Zhang met Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai on Tuesday and discussed the upcoming event, said one senior foreign ministry official. The Chinese envoy drew the attention of the foreign secretary and cautioned that the event could be used by supporters of the exiled Tibetan spiritual leader Dalai Lama, according to the official.

The envoy said some individuals could speak against China and in support of Tibet, and urged officials to make sure that no such things happen, the official told the Post.

Hundreds of researchers, scholars and experts on Tibetan studies from around the globe will gather at the event.

According to the website of the International Association of Tibetan Studies, the seminar will be organised jointly by the Himalaya Centre for Asian Studies, Kathmandu University (HiCAS, KU); and the Kathmandu University Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute (KU-CBS at RYI). The conveners are Prof Sagar Sharma (HiCAS) and Prof Thomas Doctor (KU-CBS at RYI).

Some Kathmandu-based individuals sympathetic to Beijing’s position on Tibet have also expressed concern over the event saying that promoting Tibetan language, culture and history could ultimately be interpreted as support for the Dalai Lama's views.

“Recently the government allowed Tibetan refugees to celebrate the birthday of the Dalai Lama and now this event is happening,” said one observer who has been following the Tibetan matter in Nepal. “That is why the Chinese side expressed reservations over the upcoming event.”

The Chinese ambassador, however, did not submit any written reservation or called for cancellation of the event, but voiced his concerns, the foreign ministry official told the Post.

Those who registered for the conference had to pay $360 for early registration and $440 for late registration, the Post has learnt. Registration for the event closed on June 15.

One official at the Chinese Embassy confirmed that Ambassador Zhang met with foreign secretary Rai but asked the Post to seek comment from the foreign ministry.

As per the itinerary, the opening Ceremony will be held at Kathmandu University’s Dhulikhel campus, and the rest of the programmes will be held at Hotel Soaltee.

The board members of the International Association for Tibetan Studies are Daniel Berounský (Czech Republic), Geshe Nyima Woser Choekhortshang Rinpoche (Nepal), Hildegard Diemberger (Austria), Dorji Wangchuk (Bhutan), Iwao Kazushi (Japan). Lama Jabb (UK), Pema Choedon (Norway), Karma Phuntsho (Bhutan), Françoise Pommaret (France), Jarmila Ptáčková (Czech Republic), Françoise Robin (France)., Ulrike Roesler (UK) and Yudru Tsomu (China).

Formally established in 1979 at the University of Oxford, it operates as a non-political academic body dedicated to advancing research in Tibetan history, religion, linguistics, and art.

Prof Sharma of Kathmandu University said that scholars and professors from world-renowned universities like Oxford and Cambridge will attend the conference. Scholars from 39 countries who are experts in the field of Tibetan Studies will participate.

“Its not a pro-Dalai Lama event. Huge numbers of Chinese professors and scholars are also attending. The Chinese embassy also knows about it. We have also informed different government agencies,” said Sharma.

articles.title: Supreme Court opens direct grievance channel for complaints against courts
articles.summary:
Service seekers can now lodge complaints against courts across the country directly with the judicial governance centre at the Supreme Court, a move aimed at improving accountability and addressing delays in judicial service delivery.

The centre was formally launched at the apex court on July 16, fulfilling a commitment made by Chief Justice Manoj Kumar Sharma during his parliamentary confirmation hearing to establish a grievance redressal mechanism similar to the government’s ‘Hello Sarkar’ initiative.

The facility had been operating informally since June 3. Following its formal inauguration, the centre has been providing regular services, according to Bibek Pathak, an officer at the unit.

The centre has received 186 complaints so far, with 57 percent already resolved, Pathak said.

Service delivery-related issues account for the majority of complaints, making up 55 percent of the total submissions. These include delays in serving notices, late delivery of verdicts, prolonged delays in preparing full texts of judgments, repeated postponements of hearings, cases being listed as ‘could not be heard’ or ‘cannot be heard’, delays in scheduling hearings, and prolonged transfer of case files between courts.

Other complaints relate to missing case files, hearings being scheduled on public holidays, court staff refusing or delaying the issuance of appearance dates, and requests for legal advice from litigants dissatisfied with court decisions.

In one case, a complaint was filed regarding a matter at the Kathmandu District Court that had remained pending for an extended period. The centre coordinated with Bench No. 21 of the district court and found that although the notice had been served and returned, the case had not been listed for hearing because court staff had failed to verify it. The necessary process was later completed and the case was placed on the cause list.

Similarly, after a case file went missing at the execution section of the Mahottari District Court, the centre coordinated with the court registrar to help reconstruct the file so that proceedings could resume. The registrar also sought an explanation from the employee responsible for causing difficulties for the service seeker.

In another complaint, a Supreme Court justice was accused of repeatedly assigning a case to the same bench, which eventually ruled against the petitioner. However, as the centre cannot intervene in judicial decisions or orders, the complainant was advised to seek legal remedies through consultation with a lawyer.

Chief Justice Sharma said the complaints received so far highlight the need for continuous reform to make judicial services faster, more accessible and effective.

“There were many complaints within the court system, but people had nowhere to take them. We brought this centre into operation specifically for service seekers,” Sharma told Kantipur. “People can freely raise complaints about courts without hesitation. We will make every effort to address them.”

The identities of complainants are kept confidential. Four staff members have been deployed at the centre to handle grievances, while the secretariats of the Chief Justice and Chief Registrar receive daily updates on its activities.

During the period, the centre received 27 complaints against court employees. The Chief Justice’s secretariat said action had been initiated against officials accused of misbehaviour, demanding money for services, refusing to issue appearance dates and harassing service seekers.

A total of 17 complaints were filed against judges, including allegations of failing to properly assess evidence, collusion with opposing parties and bias.

Fifteen complaints concerned the execution of judgments, including delays in dispatching field deputations (dor), intentional delays in property transfers and repeated issuance of appearance dates.

Ten complaints were unrelated to the judiciary and concerned agencies such as land revenue offices, police and local governments. Another 15 complaints lacked sufficient details, with complainants failing to provide contact numbers or case numbers.

Senior advocate Bijaya Prasad Mishra, president of the Nepal Bar Association, welcomed the establishment of the centre, saying it could strengthen transparency, good governance and service-oriented delivery within the judiciary.

“At a time when discussions on judicial reform often focus only on structural changes and appointments, a mechanism that listens to and resolves the daily problems faced by service seekers is a significant initiative,” Mishra said. “But it should not become a showcase. It must function effectively, and strict action should be taken against those who engage in wrongdoing and harass service seekers.”

Mishra said the Bar supports measures aimed at judicial reform but would not support efforts to protect insiders while placing blame only on others.

Delays in case management, hearing schedules, preparation of judgments, notice delivery and execution of court orders have long affected service seekers. Lawyers and members of the public believe a single-window system to register, analyse and resolve complaints could improve judicial services if backed by effective coordination.

“Setting up the centre alone is not enough. Its success will depend on how quickly and effectively it resolves complaints,” Mishra said. “It will serve its purpose only if it goes beyond collecting grievances by setting clear timelines for resolution, publishing regular reports and recommending policy reforms.”

articles.title: दिल्लीमा प्रहरी र विद्यार्थीबिच पुनः झडप, ढुङ्गामुढापछि अश्रुग्यास प्रहार
articles.summary:
भारतको राजधानी नयाँ दिल्लीस्थित जन्तर-मन्तरमा बुधबार राति ‘ककरोच जनता पार्टी’ (सीजेपी) का समर्थक विद्यार्थी र प्रहरीबिच पुनः उग्र झडप भएको छ।

प्रदर्शनकारीका तर्फबाट ढुङ्गामुढा भएपछि स्थिति नियन्त्रणमा लिन प्रहरीले अश्रुग्यासका गोलाहरू प्रहार गरेको छ।

सार्वजनिक भएका केही भिडियोहरूमा प्रदर्शनकारीहरूको हातमा लाठी देखिएको र उनीहरूले प्रहरीमाथि आक्रमण गरिरहेको दृश्य कैद छ।

यसअघि गत साउन ५ मा सीजेपीको संसद् मार्चका क्रममा प्रदर्शनकारीहरू संसद्को गेट नजिकै पुगेपछि उनीहरूलाई हटाउन प्रहरीले लाठीचार्ज गरेको थियो।

आन्दोलन चर्किएपछि गृह मन्त्रालयको निर्देशनसँगै पश्चिम बङ्गालको कोलकाताबाट ‘सीआरपीएफ’ का करिब २ हजार जवानलाई एयरलिफ्ट गरी दिल्ली उतारिएको छ।

सुरक्षाका कारण दिनभर बन्द गरिएका १६ वटा मेट्रो स्टेसन भने साँझदेखि पुनः सञ्चालनमा ल्याइएको छ।

articles.title: होर्मुज तनावसँगै तेल बजार प्रभावित
articles.summary:
मध्यपूर्वमा बढ्दो तनावका कारण विश्वव्यापी तेल आपूर्तिमा अवरोध आउन सक्ने चिन्ता बढेपछि बुधबार ब्रेन्ट क्रुडको मूल्य प्रतिब्यारेल ९५ अमेरिकी डलरभन्दा माथि पुगेको छ । करिब छ सातापछि पहिलोपटक ब्रेन्ट क्रुडको मूल्य यो स्तरमा पुगेको हो ।

अन्तरराष्ट्रिय बेन्चमार्क मानिने ब्रेन्ट क्रुडको मूल्य कारोबारका क्रममा केही समय प्रतिब्यारेल ९५ डलरभन्दा माथि पुगे पनि पछि केही घटेको थियो । अमेरिकी ‘वेस्ट टेक्सास इन्टरमिडियट’(डब्लुटीआई) क्रुडको मूल्यमा समेत वृद्धि देखिएको छ ।

विश्लेषकका अनुसार अमेरिका र इरानबीच पुनः चर्किएको सैन्य तनाव तथा होर्मुज र बाब अल–मान्देब जलसन्धि हुँदै हुने तेल ढुवानीमा बढेको जोखिमले बजारमा आपूर्ति अवरोधको आशङ्का बढाएको छ ।

बढ्दो भू–राजनीतिक जोखिमसँगै तत्कालीन आपूर्तिमा देखिएको कमी र कच्चा तेलको अल्पकालीन मागमा भएको वृद्धिले पनि मूल्य वृद्धिमा योगदान पु¥याएको बजार सहभागीहरूले बताएका छन् ।

पछिल्ला सातामा कच्चा तेलको मूल्यमा भएको तीव्र वृद्धिको क्रम बुधबार पनि जारी रहेको छ । विश्लेषकहरूले मध्यपूर्वको तनाव थप बढेमा भू–राजनीतिक जोखिमका कारण तेलको मूल्यमा थप दबाब पर्न सक्ने र विश्वव्यापी ऊर्जा बजार प्रभावित हुन सक्ने चेतावनी दिएका छन् ।

articles.title: राजनीतिको अन्तिम लक्ष्य नै समाजसेवा होः गगन
articles.summary:
नेपाली कांग्रेसका सभापति गगनकुमार थापाले राजनीति र धर्मको अन्तिम लक्ष्य समाजसेवा भएको बताएका छन्।

पार्टीको शुभेच्छुक संस्था नेपाल लोकतान्त्रिक होटल व्यवसायी सङ्घले बिपी कोइरालाको ४४ औँ स्मृति दिवस तथा चौँथो स्थापना दिवसको अवसरमा आज मानवसेवा आश्रममा आयोजना गरेको कार्यक्रममा उनले मानवसेवा सबैभन्दा ठूलो सेवा भएको बताए।

उनले दिन दुःखी र बेसहाराका लागि मानवसेवा आश्रमले पुर्‍याएको योगदानको उच्च प्रशंसा गरे। बिपी कोइरालाको राजनीति र धर्मसम्बन्धी दर्शनको जनकल्याण भएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

‘धर्म र राजनीति दुवैको अन्तिम लक्ष्य भनेको जनकल्याण नै हो, बिपीका अनुसार धर्मको एउटा पक्ष आध्यात्मिक हुन्छ भने अर्को पक्ष परोपकार हो, त्यसैगरी, राजनीतिको पनि मुख्य पक्ष भनेको सेवा र कल्याण नै हो,’ उनले भने। राजनीतिलाई सेवाको माध्यम बनाउनुपर्ने सभापति थापाको भनाइ थियो।

नेपाल लोकतान्त्रिक होटल व्यवसायी सङ्घका अध्यक्ष लिलाप्रसाद ढकालले सङ्घले हरेक वर्ष बिपी स्मृति दिवसको अवसरमा यस्ता सामाजिक र पुण्य काम गर्दै आइएको जानकारी दिए।

होटल व्यवसायीको काम व्यवसायसँगै समाजसेवा भएकाले आगामी दिनमा पनि यस्ता कार्यलाई निरन्तरता दिने उनको भनाइ थियो।

मानवसेवा आश्रमका संस्थापक अध्यक्ष रामजी अधिकारीले हाल देशभरका सातै प्रदेशका २३ जिल्लाका ३४ स्थानबाट मानसेवाको काम गर्दै आइरहेको जानकारी दिए।
